turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: I love a good creative challenge. Alright, let me try this out. Imagine John Smith, a busy college student, sending a quick email to his family from his iPhone. He opens his email app and types in "family@usse.com", but then realizes he needs to personalize it. He thinks for a moment and then adds "Mom and Dad" to the "To" field, but leaves the email address the same. "Why is that," you ask? In psychology, this is an example of a social cognitive theory concept called "mental framing" – we often focus on the social aspect, like the greeting, but neglect the technical details, like the email address.
